import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided as a string
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a professional style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize relationships between key features
# X-axis: Megapixels (resolution)
# Y-axis: Price (cost)
# Hue: Brand (manufacturer)
# Style: Body Type (camera form factor)
# Size: Max ISO (low-light performance indicator)
# Annotate each point with the Sensor Type for additional detail.
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='brand',
    style='body_type',
    size='max_iso',
    sizes=(50, 500), # Adjust size range for better visibility of max_iso
    palette='viridis',
    s=200, # Base size for points before 'size' mapping
    edgecolor='black',
    alpha=0.8
)

# Add text labels for 'sensor_type' to each point
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    plt.text(
        row['megapixels'] + 0.5, # Offset x-coordinate slightly
        row['price_usd'] + 50,  # Offset y-coordinate slightly
        f"{row['sensor_type']}",
        fontsize=9,
        color='dimgray',
        ha='left',
        va='bottom'
    )

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Camera Specifications: Megapixels vs. Price by Brand and Body Type', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement and appearance
plt.legend(title='Camera Details', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot as output.png
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300)
